Sam Carter: quick update from the queueing-policy ablation runs I kicked off this morning :eyes:
Sam Carter: tl;dr — turning on `sticky_batching=true` improves steady-state throughput slightly (+2%) but increases tail latency for bursty small-request workloads (p95 +6%). KV-cache hit-rate dropped ~3% in those bursts which lines up with worse merging behavior. more details below.
Dmitri Petrov: can you paste the prom queries you used? also what workload (qps, seq len distribution)?
Sam Carter: workload = mixed-prod-replay-2026-01 (70% short, 30% long, seq median 48 tokens). qps ~ 1200 on canary. promQLs I used:
```
# batch utilization: fraction of non-empty microbatches
sum(rate(batcher_microbatch_bytes_used[1m])) / sum(rate(batcher_microbatch_capacity_bytes[1m]))

# queue depth (per-batcher pod)
sum(batcher_queue_length) by (pod)

# tokens/sec observed
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[30s]))
```
Mia Chen: confirmed the KV hit-rate dip — sticky keeps requests in the same microbatch so we see fewer cross-request KV merges, hence more redundant recompute for long sequences. can we test a hybrid? sticky only if seq_len < X or if queue_age < Y?
Priya Rao: yeah, that's the ablation I wanted to try — policy knobs:
- `sticky_batching` boolean
- `sticky_max_seq_tokens` (int)
- `sticky_max_queue_age_ms` (int)
We should test three ablations: always-on, always-off, hybrid heuristics (seq threshold & queue-age gating).
Carol Nguyen: for telemetry we'll need new panels: batch_utilization by seq_len bucket, queue_age histogram (0..200ms), token/sec broken down by batch-size. Also add a regression alert: p95 latency up >4% vs baseline over 10m.
Zane Patel: sharing the lightweight flame for the p95 regression run — looks like kernel selection shifted because sticky increases opportunities for microbatched GEMM reuse but also longer KV-cache churn. snippet from perf profiler:
```
# top hotspots (canary run)
0.  kernel_gemm_qkv_fused  31.2%  (was 28.7% baseline)
1.  kv_cache_merge         18.6%  (was 15.0% baseline)
2.  transformer_attn       12.4%  (unchanged)
```
Mia Chen: interesting that GEMM time went up — maybe larger contiguous batches changed kernel selection thresholds and picked a slower kernel for long sequences. we should capture kernel selection traces when we flip sticky.
Sam Carter: steps I'm proposing:
1) add the three ablation variants to canary (traffic slice 3%).
2) wire up the new grafana panels (Carol) and prom queries (above).
3) capture kernel-selection trace + perf profiler for 30m for each variant.
4) compare token/sec, p95 latency, kv-hit-rate, batch-utilization and kernel hotspots.
Priya Rao: for rollout config, also include `max_wait_ms` and `batch_size_floor` so we don't starve small requests. suggest default hybrid: `sticky=true, sticky_max_seq_tokens=64, sticky_max_queue_age_ms=8, max_wait_ms=12`.
ops-bot: deploy/canary/attach-config succeeded for service=batcher-canary (cid: bc-2026-04-03-14) :white_check_mark:
Dmitri Petrov: thanks — can we also log per-request metadata `seq_len` and `batch_bucket` in the sampling pipeline (1% sample) so we can correlate latency -> batch composition?
Sam Carter: yes, will add that sampling flag. I'll upload the raw experiment notebook and grafana snapshots to the canary thread later. planning to run ablations for 2 hours each.
Carol Nguyen: I'll create the dashboard panels now and share link (grafana/d/xyz/batcher-ablation) once ready. also adding alert rule: `p95_latency > baseline_p95 * 1.04 for 10m`
Zane Patel: small note — when we compute batch_utilization make sure to account for prefix caching: reported 'used' bytes should exclude cached-prefix hits or we'll undercount effective reuse.
Sam Carter: good call, will adjust prom target to subtract cached prefix tokens.
Priya Rao: if hybrid shows wins, we can roll to 20% and monitor. if p95 stays up even with hybrid, we'll revert.
Sam Carter: ok will post results thread + decision doc. thanks all :chart_with_upwards_trend:
